what_happened: An the person running Athena saw in the drain log that the batch-ordering test "a group of urgent items does not start ahead of the improvement turn" failed twice (11 Nov 02:20 UTC critic-challenge job, and about 22:10 UTC). Both jobs did not touch the drain. Each time the test shard "did not finish". The the person running Athena suspects the test is slow or timing-dependent. The earlier error review had already said the kept output does not show why it failed. Whole jobs were lost as a result. No job id is recorded on the event.
cause: A test shard that does not finish leaves no record of which test hung or how long it ran. Nothing separates a hang or timeout from a real assertion failure. Nothing tracks a test that fails on unrelated jobs, so a flaky or slow test rejects correct work and nobody can tell why. The kept output is too thin to diagnose from.
other_causes: The test may depend on timing or machine load, so it fails when jobs run in parallel or the disk is busy.
No flaky-test quarantine, re-run or baseline check against main exists. Failures on jobs that did not touch the code are not recognised as unrelated to the job.
open_hypotheses: The test is timing-dependent or slow. The fields do not confirm this.
The shard may be killed by a shard-level or job-level time limit, or by resource exhaustion, rather than by this test itself.
Both failures may share an environment cause such as load or low disk. The fields cannot show this.
prevention: When a test shard does not finish, keep the name of the running test, its elapsed time and the last output lines, and record the stop as a timeout rather than a test failure. Re-run a timed-out shard once on its own, and report any test that fails on a job that did not touch its code as a suspected flaky test, not as a job failure. With that, a hanging test is named at once and its fix is diagnosed from evidence, not guessed. All gate disagreement counts are 0, so no gate is relaxed or removed.
proposed_request: Diagnose and fix the test 'a group of urgent items does not start ahead of the improvement turn', which fails with its test shard 'did not finish' in jobs that did not touch the drain (11 Nov 02:20 UTC critic-challenge job and about 22:10 UTC). Outcome: (1) State the root cause, from a measured run of the test alone, repeated and also under load. Say whether it is slow, hangs, or depends on timing or the clock. (2) Fix that cause, not a symptom, so the test passes every time in 20 repeated runs and finishes well within the shard limit. (3) When a test shard does not finish, record the running test's name, elapsed time and last output lines in the kept check output, and mark the result as a timeout. Add a test for that recording. Add a CHANGELOG.md entry.
